proposal.hypothesis: The measured two-group schedule was slower than baseline (82.32 µs versus 55.00 µs), while the measured four-group schedule was also slower but less so (63.81 µs). A three-group scalar unroll tests whether intermediate lookup concurrency reduces loop overhead without the four-group schedule's larger live-value set; register pressure and the combined validity check may still outweigh any benefit.

retained: Unrolled the table-driven decode loop to process three independent eight-character groups per bulk iteration, interleaving scalar lookups across groups.
Required at least 28 remaining input characters before processing 24, reserving a quartet for scalar padding, tail, and invalid-input handling.
Used one combined validity check before stores so invalid blocks fall through to the existing scalar decoder without changing output semantics.
Added no explicit SIMD, parallel execution, benchmark-length specialization, or changes outside src/candidate.cpp.
